quest.title: The Fond Farewell
quest.description: The ancient god was subdued once again following a fierce battle and much sacrifice. The dust settles, and your journey in Liyue is reaching its conclusion with the Rite of Parting. But before that, there are still some mysteries regarding the Geo Archon that need unraveling.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x750, Primogem x30, Mora x35925, Memory of Immovable Crystals x1, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it... finally over?

dialogues.speaker: Moon Carver
dialogues.text: The ominous aura of that monster has indeed begun to fade.

dialogues.speaker: Moon Carver
dialogues.text: The effects of the Sigil of Permission last but a short time.

dialogues.speaker: Moon Carver
dialogues.text: It will be some time before the Overlord of the Vortex can make any waves again.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: We are indebted to you for your assistance. If the adepti hadn't happened to be here, the future of Liyue Harbor would surely have been in great jeopardy...

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: Hmph, save your flattery. We didn't just "happen" to be here... Surely you won't pretend to have forgotten the reason for which we came?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Come now, there's no need for such harsh words, Cloud Retainer.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: I've heard that when Ningguang began learning to do business, she had already started setting aside part of her then-limited income in preparation for building the Jade Chamber.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: At first, it was only the size of a small room. But with continued expansion, it has become the palace that lies before you now.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: It is a testament to Ningguang's entire life, both as a businesswoman and as the backbone of the Liyue Qixing.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Seeing the Jade Chamber destroyed in the defense of Liyue means much to her. To me, such cooperation and sacrifice deserves at least some recognition, don't you agree?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Well, I was really hoping you would say that such sacrifice could at least be used as some leverage in our negotiations.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: ...Heh.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Thank you all for hearing me out. We know very well why the adepti came here today... But please forgive us, we cannot yield to your wishes.

dialogues.speaker: Moon Carver
dialogues.text: Oh?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: 3,700 years... According to our records, the adepti signed a contract with Rex Lapis to protect Liyue 3,700 years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Even to this very day, Liyue and its lands have stood the test of time, immovable as stone, just as it was thousands of years before. This is truly no small feat.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: But that does not mean that the Liyue of today is the same city as it was all those years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Do not merely cast your protective gaze upon the land. Instead, focus your sights on our city and each of the citizens that dwell within it.

dialogues.speaker: Moon Carver
dialogues.text: Are you questioning our means of protecting Liyue?

dialogues.speaker: Mountain Shaper
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: I mean no offense. I simply hope that our adepti forebearers would see Liyue in a new light.

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: Hah, "forebearers" you say. One doubts you would be fit to be part of such a lineage...

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: This morning, Rex Lapis appeared to me in a dream.

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: In the dream, I yearned to tell him that we Qixing, though mortal, are equally bound to the contract. Each passing generation of the Qixing leaves many things of value to be inherited by the next generation.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: I also thought to tell him how the past generations of Qixing had strove under his rule to survive in our mortal world, establishing a network of contracts which has since come to be known as "trade."

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: But I dared not speak. I could only gaze at him in silence until the moment I awoke.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, Ningguang...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're all on the same side here...

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: Yet another perspective... What are you trying to say, Outlander?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: When there is discord between the guardians and those they were meant to defend...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Harmony becomes very difficult to restore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, that's something that happened in Mondstadt — it's a story about the Four Winds and the people of the Anemo Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Anemo Archon sought to quell the strife between the two sides, because he believed that such conflict would only scar the hearts of both and that nothing good would come of it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is what we learned in the City of Freedom.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Each of the Seven Nations has its own scars from the past.

dialogues.speaker: Mountain Shaper
dialogues.text: Though your point is the very height of simplicity...

dialogues.speaker: Mountain Shaper
dialogues.text: As adepti, we've become a laughingstock, to be chastised thus by an outlander who has lent us such succor.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Alright, alright. Didn't Ningguang suggest that we should focus on the city and each of its citizens? I know I already have, so why not see for yourselves?

dialogues.speaker: Fengyan
dialogues.text: I apologize for appearing in full armor. I'm afraid I cannot show the proper courtesies.

dialogues.speaker: Moon Carver
dialogues.text: And who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Fengyan
dialogues.text: I am Fengyan, a sergeant of the Millelith. I have come to extend my thanks to the adepti.

dialogues.speaker: Fengyan
dialogues.text: I thought this battle would perhaps be my last. But thanks to the aid of the adepti, our forces were not as badly battered as I feared we might be.

dialogues.speaker: Fengyan
dialogues.text: Although I am a mere mortal soldier, I promise to hold the line and never betray the grace given to us by the illuminated adepti this day.

dialogues.speaker: Changchang
dialogues.text: Huh? Why does everyone look so down? Didn't we just beat that big monster?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Hahaha! Weren't you frightened, dear? It was quite the predicament...

dialogues.speaker: Changchang
dialogues.text: I wasn't afraid. All the strong Millelith guards were there, and those powerful heroes with their Visions were there... Everyone was there!

dialogues.speaker: Changchang
dialogues.text: When danger is near, everyone always protects me. And the rest of the time, they make fun toys, and tasty snacks, and... and loads of things that make the harbor so pretty!

dialogues.speaker: Changchang
dialogues.text: Thanks for protecting Liyue Harbor! Please come visit us for the next Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, we wouldn't be able to participate.

dialogues.speaker: Changchang
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Because we are adepti.

dialogues.speaker: Changchang
dialogues.text: Oh, okay... It must be hard being an adeptus.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aww...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: You see, this is what Liyue is like today.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: The country of contracts is grateful to the adepti for their protection. But it is no longer necessary for the city to rely on the adepti's power to solve every little niggling matter.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Although their blood is weak, there is still strength to be found in those we call mortals...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: The time of contracts between gods and Liyue has long since passed. Now is the time of contracts between Liyue and its people.

dialogues.speaker: Mountain Shaper
dialogues.text: Hmm, seeing the port around us now, it is hard not to feel a bit out of place... wouldn't you say so, Cloud Retainer?

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: Your line of inquiry is askew. One did not spearhead this expedition to Liyue Harbor...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... seems like the adepti have had a change of heart.

choices.text: They've listened to what the people have said.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Let us return now.

response.speaker: Moon Carver
response.text: ...Eager to leave, Conqueror of Demons?

response.speaker: Madame Ping
response.text: Hehehe...

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: Yes, one understands what the Conqueror of Demons means. The city of Liyue has changed much after our long separation.

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: One fears that by the time one finally grasps the new contracts of Liyue, you humans would have once again changed the place beyond recognition.

response.speaker: Mountain Shaper
response.text: Fair enough. Away we shall, and return whence we came...

response.speaker: Moon Carver
response.text: Hmph...

response.speaker: Moon Carver
response.text: Since we adepti have consensus, then one shall persist no further.

response.speaker: Moon Carver
response.text: But how will we ensure that the Liyue Qixing will not simply exploit their power once we depart? In my view, that is still a thing to be guarded against...

response.speaker: Ningguang
response.text: *chuckles*

response.speaker: Madame Ping
response.text: Alright, Moon Carver. You needn't worry. It seems to me that this right of supervision is best left to the people of Liyue.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whew... Looks like the conflict between humans and adepti was avoided. All's well that ends well, huh?

choices.text: You can say that again...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! It's nice that we've got peace and all, but we're forgetting one thing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Childe wanted to unleash the god so he could lure Rex Lapis out!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But we were able to handle the Overlord of the Vortex on our own... So Rex Lapis never showed up!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and speaking of that — don't we still need to get to the bottom of that archon's "death," too?

choices.text: The adepti were quite reasonable in the end...
And they're trying to understand things from their perspective.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Is there anything I can do for you two? I'm afraid that Wangsheng Funeral Parlor isn't in the best state to receive guests.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've come to see Zhongli. Could you please tell him we're here?

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, Zhongli isn't here at the moment. It seems he went to Northland Bank.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Doesn't the Northland Bank belong to the Fatui?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Last time we saw Zhongli was before we went to the Golden House...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think he doesn't know about the attack on Liyue? Visiting the Fatui at a time like this could only mean more trouble!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We had better go and make sure that everything is okay.

talks.objective: Look for Zhongli at Northland Bank

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: The clean-up of the premises, managing the crowds as they exit, making an account of the Rite... There's much that remains to be done. I didn't miss anything, did I?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: You call this "cooperation between Harbingers"? Cooperation involves communication, you know...

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Hehe, don't take it to heart, Childe. Besides, aren't you happy that you got to skip the formalities and bring chaos to the land? I'm sure you must've enjoyed that...

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: ...Oh, it seems that some of your friends have arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, it's Zhongli and Childe! And... you! You're also one of the Harbingers...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Signora!

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Haha, it's you two. I believe we've met once before... In the City of Bards, was it? I'm glad you still remember my name.

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Ah, right. I imagine that it must have been rather hard to forget watching helplessly as something precious was snatched away from your friend.

choices.text: (Breathe... Just stay calm.)

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: #Well, if it isn't {NICKNAME}. This is our first time seeing each other since Liyue was nearly wiped off the map. This is certainly a bit... awkward, wouldn't you say?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph, Paimon knew that we should never have trusted a Fatui Harbinger!

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Aw, now don't say that. Sure, I may have misled you, but I never had anything against you personally...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Besides, I thought we were getting along quite well together, didn't you? Except for that little tussle we had at the end... Haha.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Nothing personal, we just have... different views, that's all. Of course, you may very well hold this against me, but that's up to you...

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: The real deceivers here are Signora and Zhongli... curse them for leading me on.

choices.text: Zhongli tricked you?

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: So actually, I think—

response.speaker: Signora
response.text: Stop wasting time, Childe. There'll be plenty of time to chat once I'm through here.

response.speaker: Signora
response.text: You remember the agreement, Morax. Now, if you would be so kind... The Gnosis, please.

choices.text: Agreement?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What in the world are you talking about!?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The contract is fulfilled. That which thou seeketh is now bestowed unto thee, for my promise is solid as stone.

response.speaker: Signora
response.text: Hmph, how sanctimonious...

choices.text: So Zhongli is actually Rex Lapis?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What! So you're the Lord of Geo!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, wait! That's an exciting twist and all — but why give the Gnosis to the Fatui!?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I do not give it for free. I give it as agreed upon in the contract... for it is a matter solely between the Tsaritsa and I.

choices.text: I'm afraid I don't understand...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you don't think you went a little bit too far with that whole fake death thing!? Everyone was preparing the ceremony for you when splat, this big dragon falls out of the sky and all of Liyue goes into an uproar. Talk about a disaster!

response.speaker: Signora
response.text: Hehe... Gathering all the forces that had been bubbling behind the scenes, and then stirring them together in a pot that was bound to boil over... That's what he wanted to see, am I right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait... what?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Perhaps it's best that I explain.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: As you know, I've dwelt upon this world for more than six thousand years. It is now 3,700 years ago that I founded Liyue together with the adepti.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Even boulders that can withstand whirlpools will erode with the passing of time. I kept convincing myself that cracks had not begun to form and that the end of my time had not yet come.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Until one drizzly day, as I was strolling along the harbor, I heard a merchant tell one of his workers, "You've finished your duties, go ahead and call it a day."

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I stood motionless among the crowds, asking myself, "Have I already finished my duties?"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Zhongli...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: But as I began to consider relinquishing my divine role, I soon discovered that many reasons still remained to not hastily depart.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Was Liyue, the city I had dwelt in for so long, already prepared to enter its next age? I decided that a test was needed in order to reveal the answer.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: So I feigned my own death, and gathered the cast of Childe, the adepti, and the Liyue Qixing to play their roles together on the stage that was Liyue.

choices.text: So, were you satisfied with the finale?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Indeed, I was. The Gnosis which I had kept for so many years suddenly seemed to have lost its meaning.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you mean that if the chaos ever reached the point of no return, you would simply appear and use your divine powers to bring Liyue back under control?

response.speaker: Signora
response.text: Of course. And it would have been all too easy for him, too.

response.speaker: Signora
response.text: Just as a child quickly matures after losing their parents, so has Liyue matured when faced with the death of its deity...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: In the end, the resolution to all that has transpired was even more satisfactory than I could have hoped for.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Take the adepti, for instance. Owing to their years of seclusion, they were the least informed. Yet, when faced with a crisis, they, commendably, showed the greatest amount of restraint possible. Not only did they manage to co-operate with the Qixing, but in the end, they even made efforts to understand the hearts of the people.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Credit is also due to Signora, the emissary dispatched by the Cryo Archon to fulfill our contract. At my request, she kept everything she knew in strict confidence — this despite the eavesdropping ears of her colleague, Childe.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: This meant I could remain as Zhongli, even having the chance to fulfill the age-old traditions of Liyue in this mortal form. Thank you for joining me on this journey, Traveler.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: All of these things turned out as I had planned. There is only one thing that I had not anticipated... and that was the conduct of the Liyue Qixing.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I had expected them to do no more than the adepti... To come to the defense of Liyue. But when all was said and done...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: They seized the opportunity to supplant Liyue's divine protectors, and used the subsequent power vacuum left by my death to quickly gain complete control of Liyue.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? That doesn't sound good at all!

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Hah... On the contrary, I think it is excellent. I had always feared that it was too soon for them to take over from me, and it was also that which I longed for the most. As such, this is the best parting gift anyone could have given this god of old.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Hey, what about me? Doesn't anyone feel the least bit of remorse for deceiving me? You've practically kept me in the dark!

response.speaker: Signora
response.text: Heh, I think that thanks would be more appropriate. You certainly played no small part in all of this... Wreaking havoc and turning the city upside down. The Lord of Geo ought to thank you for your performance, if anything.

response.speaker: Signora
response.text: If you hadn't created the pressure of a battle between mortals, adepti and a god, the lump of coal resting in the hands of the Geo Archon — Liyue — would never have been able to become a dazzling diamond of a city.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Huh? Just whose side are you on, mocking me like that? Are you itching for a fight?

choices.text: We were both equally fooled.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Be that as it may, you've come out of this as the hero of Liyue. I, on the other hand, will be forever proscribed as a disturber of the peace, no?

response.speaker: Signora
response.text: Heh... Well then, with the Gnosis in my possession, I have no use for such idle chatter. We should return to Zapolyarny Palace and seek an audience with Her Majesty, the Tsaritsa. Come, Childe.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Ugh, fine... I'll meet you there later. I'm not sharing a boat with the likes of you.

response.speaker: Signora
response.text: Hmph, do as you wish.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Now then, is there anything else you wish to ask me?

choices.text: I'd like to know what the Cryo Archon offered you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! As Zhongli always told us, "a good trade is a fair trade." Paimon has no idea what could be a good trade for a Gnosis.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Realistically speaking, there is no such thing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh???

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: However, I am the God of Contracts. For thousands of years, I have made countless contracts. If the deal was of no benefit, then I certainly would not be inclined to agree to it.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: My agreement with the Cryo Archon will be the last of my contracts as the Geo Archon — my "contract to end all contracts."

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: As for the bargaining chip that the Tsaritsa used to balance the scales...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Uncover that answer for yourself in your future journeys.

choices.text: What could possibly be worth a Gnosis?
You've really embarrassed yourself this time.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: Hey! Haven't you learned the Liyue saying? "Don't always call it as you see it"!

choices.text: Let me guess — you had another plan in case it all burned down.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: That's right, which is why I continued to safeguard the Gnosis until now.

choices.text: And why did you feign your death?
I mean, I did have my suspicions...
Gnosis?
Signora and Zhongli?
I still have time to take it back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #No, don't let her get to you, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've yet to gather the powers of all seven elements, and our last battle at the Golden House was almost more than you could handle...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So it might be best to keep things peaceful this time, seeing that two of the Harbingers are here.

talks.objective: Follow the road up to Yujing Terrace

dialogues.speaker: Big-Footed Dajiao
dialogues.text: ...Well, since we're going through with this Rite of Parting... I guess it means that those rumors hit the nail on the head.

dialogues.speaker: Wrench Wang
dialogues.text: So Rex Lapis is really... But they didn't catch the culprit, did they?

dialogues.speaker: Big-Footed Dajiao
dialogues.text: Ah, come on, do you think that the assassin could have been a normal person? You know what I think? I don't think any of the gossip on the streets you hear from those shady types is worth anything.

dialogues.speaker: Big-Footed Dajiao
dialogues.text: There's only one real possibility in my mind. I've heard that the assassin was that Fatui fellow. Youngish, pretty high in rank — I think they called him Childe.

dialogues.speaker: Wrench Wang
dialogues.text: The Fatui? They certainly are very suspicious. Who knows what those greedy, crooked folks...

dialogues.speaker: Big-Footed Dajiao
dialogues.text: Shh! Lower your voice! If the Fatui catch you in their sights, Rex Lapis won't be around to protect you this time!

talks.objective: Follow the road up to Yujing Terrace

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Gao
dialogues.text: You know that god from the ocean couldn't have just shown up out of nowhere. I mean, it's been two thousand years since Rex Lapis subdued it.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Sun
dialogues.text: Yes, and to think that this happened right on the heels of the incident with Rex Lapis, too...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Gao
dialogues.text: Say, do you think the person who assassinated our Lord and released that evil god might have been one and the same?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Sun
dialogues.text: Now that you mention it, that's very possible. Yes... it's very possible indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Sun
dialogues.text: I mean, it all fits together! That person must have colluded with the evil god to harm Rex Lapis. Ugh, that wicked, black-hearted scoundrel...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Sun
dialogues.text: Still, what sort of supernatural prowess must this person possess to be able to do such things? I have never heard of such a person in all my years.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Gao
dialogues.text: Ah, forget it. Guessing's no use to us. Look, the Millelith over there looks like he's about to make an announcement. Let's hear what the Ministry of Civil Affairs has to say first.

dialogues.speaker: Fengyan
dialogues.text: Hear ye all the Qixing's words:

dialogues.speaker: Fengyan
dialogues.text: Though a dragon soars ageless as the mountains, it too must return to dust. This is common knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Fengyan
dialogues.text: Gods and adepti live glorious lives, but both light and shadow have their season. So, too, must they face divinely-appointed trials.

dialogues.speaker: Fengyan
dialogues.text: Rumors and hearsay abound on the streets that Rex Lapis was murdered. Now, let the truth be revealed.

dialogues.speaker: Fengyan
dialogues.text: Having been thwarted in his trial, Rex Lapis' soul has recouped the celestial heights. He beseeches the people of Liyue to grieve not, and to let not their hearts be saddened.

dialogues.speaker: Fengyan
dialogues.text: Nor are they to believe street-borne rumors or indulge in baseless speculation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ah... Um, Paimon needs a translation on what the Qixing's announcement said, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: They said that Rex Lapis wasn't murdered.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...So that's how they're spinning it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Something feels off. Why would they suddenly give up looking for the murderer? Not to mention how this excuse sounds like something they just made up on the spot.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could the Qixing already have known that Rex Lapis wasn't dead? But Zhongli said that neither they nor the adepti knew anything...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Did Zhongli tell them in secret after his Gnosis changed hands?

choices.text: That's possible.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly, right? Ooh, seems like the Rite of Parting has been going on for a while now. Let's go have a look.

choices.text: I think you've hit the bull's-eye this time.
They said that Rex Lapis died because of a divine trial.

talks.objective: Go to the site of the Rite of Parting

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, it's Ningguang and Keqing. Are they saying something? Are their speeches over?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: ...As said previously, Rex Lapis' soul returning to the heavens is the end of the contract, and it is also the end of an era.

dialogues.speaker: Shitou
dialogues.text: 3,700 years of contracts, burnt and reduced to ash...

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: We, the people of Liyue were indeed prosperous. But blinded by our prosperity, we forgot that time can be pitiless.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: The long, unending dream of our archon walking among us...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Mm...

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Now that we have awoken from our dream, we must learn to say farewell.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Will you stand with us as we reestablish our contracts — as we build a new age of prosperity?

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: So concludes the words of her Eminence, the Tianquan.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Does Her Eminence the Yuheng have anything to add?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Is she looking this way?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes! She really is looking our way!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Is that the traveler who they say defeated the ancient god?

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: So young...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: The Liyue Qixing always repay their debts. And as you have heard, our eyes see far and our reach is long.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Name your price. You deserve that much.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well... could you help me put up some missing person posters...?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: As for the mortals and adepti of Liyue... what shape shall our relationship take from now on?

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Ha, and to think I'd put my best perfume on before coming here, thinking you'd like it...

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: But it seems as if those perfumes really were meant to be offered to Rex Lapis.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Well, that's fine. Suffer no rivals in love, they say, and that's three gone in one stroke. *chuckles*

dialogues.speaker: Shitou
dialogues.text: Ah, Rex Lapis... Rex Lapis...

dialogues.speaker: Shitou
dialogues.text: Hmm. Now that I think about it, if everyone's of the same mind as me...

dialogues.speaker: Shitou
dialogues.text: Perhaps mementos for Rex Lapis might be the best short-term business opportunity...

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Roping you in was possibly the most masterful move we could have made. I believe that future generations will say so too, when our deeds come up for their review.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Heh. Why, you... Were you just trying to look cool earlier, or are you really that selfless?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: If you were looking for someone, you could have just told me that in private...

talks.objective: Talk to the people taking part in the rite
Look for Zhongli at the scene

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Zhongli!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look at this. Everyone in Liyue's caught up in their emotions, thinking that they'll never see Rex Lapis again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...And here you are, looking all relaxed!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Hahaha. Why would I not feel more at ease after laying down the burden I have borne for 3,700 years?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Right, if the two of you can spare the time, I should treat you to a meal at the Xinyue Kiosk.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hah! That sounds like big talk, Zhongli. Paimon might have believed you if you were treating us to some Third-Round Knockout, but you'd have to pay out your nose just to stand inside Xinyue Kiosk. Are you sure you can afford it?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: You're right, I do lack the Mora.

choices.text: You've been this way this entire time, but...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why would Morax lack Mora?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: As the Rex Lapis Morax, I can easily create Mora. But since I have chosen to walk this earth as the mortal Zhongli, I should abide by the same rules that mortals do.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: When I was journeying with you, though I still had the Gnosis in hand, I knew that I must soon retire from my role as an archon. So I had to... rehearse a little, for my new life.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, no wonder! Paimon gets it now. You didn't look at the price tags when we were spending because you've never had to.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But since you weren't used to not being able to just make more Mora as and when you wanted to, you had to try becoming a parasite to society who lives off of other peoples' credit...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Well, we were only spending Fatui money. You don't have to say it like that...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: In the city of commerce, we do not merely exchange money or goods. We also exchange knowledge, memories, and foresight, as well as positions, roles, and lives.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The archon Morax could never experience life as the true mortal Zhongli could, no matter how many times he descended to be with his people.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: #Haha, I must thank you for that, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I will treasure the memories that I made as Zhongli, traveling the streets of Liyue with you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It was a fine journey.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: That is true, but there is no journey that does not end. No meetings without partings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm... Paimon thinks that we should make a move and continue our search for The Seven.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I fear that continuing your journey may be difficult. The nation that neighbors Liyue by sea, Inazuma, is presently closed.

choices.text: "Closed"?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Yes. The nation has been closed by order of its deity.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The Electro Archon, Baal — and just as the people of Liyue preferred to call me Rex Lapis, she too goes by another name among locals in Inazuma.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, Paimon thinks we've heard that one before. Uh.. Rai... Raiden?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: That is the case. And since Raiden is also the Shogun of Inazuma, people call her the Raiden Shogun.

choices.text: The Inazuma Shogunate...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, though people at the wharf were saying that the situation in Inazuma is very tense, Paimon doesn't remember that always being the case. It wasn't that bad last year...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Zhongli, since you're Rex Lapis, shouldn't you know something about what's happening there? Just how did Inazuma become a closed nation?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It's because of Visions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Visions?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: When faced with circumstances beyond their control, humans often bemoan their lack of power.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: But if a person shows true strength of will at a desperate and fateful moment in their life, the gods will look upon them with favor.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: This is what Visions are. Magical foci bestowed upon those who have been acknowledged by the gods.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh. That's how people in Teyvat see it.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: But starting from last year, the Raiden Shogun began promulgating the "Vision Hunt Decree."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Vision Hunt Decree?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Yes. It was an order to seize all Visions within Inazuma's borders, and to inlay them upon the hands of the Statue of the Omnipresent God.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They want to seize Visions? But why? Aren't Visions blessings from the gods?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I should think that in the Raiden Shogun's eyes, it is precisely because they are divine blessings, that they should be under the sole dominion of divinity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa... That's harsh.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The Anemo Archon is the God of Freedom, and the Geo Archon is the God of Contracts. For her part, the Raiden Shogun is the God of Eternity. It seems as though she has finally decided to eliminate any unstable elements that could pose a threat to her eternal realm.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The fact that even I, the oldest of The Seven, have now "passed away" will only strengthen her resolve to pursue eternity.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Knowing her, she must have again quoted that adage she is most fond of when proclaiming that decree to her people:

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: "Seven ideals for seven gods, and of these, Eternity is nearest unto the Heavenly Principles."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Heavenly Principles...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Alright, then. Was there anything else you wished to know?

choices.text: So, about the "trial..."

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Haha... Ah, that was a good one. Failing a divine trial? How they came up with that excuse, I will never know.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: That said, the reason why the Qixing were so eager to resolve the incident and stop pursuing the culprit was indeed because they received news in secret that Rex Lapis was not dead.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I hinted as much to the adepti as well.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: How did I accomplish that, you ask? Hmm... Have you ever heard of this particularly convenient adepti art known as "gifting dreams and visions"?

choices.text: What about Childe...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, about that. Before the Qixing made their announcement, we listened to a lot of people talking on the way. Most of them put the blame for everything on Childe.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: These are indeed false accusations, but it remains undeniably true that Childe did send people to the Jade Chamber to prevent the adepti and the Qixing from defeating the ancient god.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I've heard that Ningguang is busy milking that for all it's worth on the foreign relations front at the moment, browbeating the envoys of the Fatui...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Ah, those poor Snezhnayan diplomats. If it were not for Childe's exalted position as a Harbinger, I'm certain that they would have shifted all the blame to him and called for his dismissal by now.

choices.text: As for the Liyue Qixing...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: "The time of the adepti has long passed. If even the Liyue Qixing don't want to face that truth, then what future is there for Liyue?"

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Keqing is absolutely right in saying this.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Now, though I did laud Ningguang's desire for power, believing this to be a good thing, and thought as a matter of course that she must have been behind the Qixing's plan to take governing power over Liyue from the hands of the gods and adepti...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Could the original person who brought up the idea of seizing power have been...? Hmm...

choices.text: Now, about Mora...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! Zhongli, now that you don't have your Gnosis, what's going to happen to all the Mora in Teyvat?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Since Morax is "dead," are they all just gonna disappear?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, isn't the Golden House the only mint in the entire continent? Will it even continue to work?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: The Mora present now will not vanish. But the Golden House will indeed have to cease operations for a lengthy period of time, since creating Mora requires the use of the Geo Archon's power.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Argh! This is terrible. We're all about to run out of Mora! The world is coming to an end!

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Yes, this is indeed a major issue from a financial standpoint...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Uh... Well. I suppose we'll just leave such troublesome matters to the Liyue Qixing to debate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then... did you at least set some private funds aside for yourself?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Oh, a private fund? Hmm, this does seem like a good, logical, common-sense idea.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Ah, it's a shame...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's a shame?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It's a shame that I didn't think of it at the time.

choices.text: There's nothing else...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Well then, I suppose you'll have to find a way to get inside this closed nation. Have patience... I suspect that some serendipity must first come into play...

choices.text: The Shogun...
Who's the god who rules Inazuma?
But why would Morax lack Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Observe the Noctilucous Jade
dialogues.text: (Azure and bright, it does no shame to the name of radiant grade Noctilucous Jade. Very elegant indeed.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe the kites
dialogues.text: (The seven kites used in the ceremony, which represent The Seven.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe the kites
dialogues.text: #(How long before I find the one who took my {F#brother}{M#sister}?)

dialogues.speaker: Observe the censer
dialogues.text: (Everlasting Incense... The lengths we went to to get our hands on that. The powders made from Glaze Lilies still remain at the bottom.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe the censer
dialogues.text: (Two million, nine-hundred-and-ninety thousand Mora's worth of incense, going up in smoke... Ugh...)

dialogues.speaker: Observe the perfume
dialogues.text: (A specially prepared perfume, made from a exotic type of Silk Flower. It has a faint scent.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe the perfume
dialogues.text: (Still, why would Rex Lapis go for the scent preferred by older women...)

dialogues.speaker: Observe the bell
dialogues.text: (As per the traditions of the Rite of Parting, the cleansing sound of the bell sees the soul of the immortal on its way.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe the bell
dialogues.text: (It's hard to believe someone would store such a precious object in a teapot filled with cobwebs.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe the Noctilucous Jade
dialogues.text: (Azure and bright, it does no shame to the name of radiant grade Noctilucous Jade. Very elegant indeed.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe the Noctilucous Jade
dialogues.text: (Azure and bright, it does no shame to the name of radiant grade Noctilucous Jade. Very elegant indeed.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe the Noctilucous Jade
dialogues.text: (Azure and bright, it does no shame to the name of radiant grade Noctilucous Jade. Very elegant indeed.)

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Oh? Why are you hanging back here? Don't you want to get closer to the action?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: You went through a lot to organize this rite, and this is a rare opportunity to see your journey bear fruit with your own eyes. You should make the most of it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon... can't... absorb so much information at once...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, Zhongli, what sort of contract did you sign with the Cryo Archon? Paimon's so curious!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: ...One of the clauses of our contract was not to divulge any of its contents.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... You're so petty.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Come to think of it, I wonder what business Mr. Zhongli has at the Northland Bank? He didn't tell me, either...
